title: qBraid Unveils qBraid OS and Launches Hosted GH200 GPU Simulators at NVIDIA GTC Berlin - Quantum Computing Report
gist: qBraid unveiled qBraid OS, an agentic operating system for QPU scheduling, metering and real-time QEC decoding built on NVIDIA CUDA-Q and NVQLink, and launched hosted GH200 simulators: gpu-sv up to 35 qubits (2.7 s versus 2 min 43 s on 32 CPU cores for a 32-qubit circuit) and gpu-tn up to 500 qubits.

insights.claim: qBraid introduced qBraid OS, an agentic operating system for quantum hardware makers and supercomputing centers to manage, schedule and operate QPUs, unveiled at NVIDIA GTC Berlin.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Software layers for QPU operation are becoming a distinct product category.

insights.claim: qBraid OS is positioned to replace fragmented, custom-built quantum control stacks with an integrated framework spanning account management, job queue scheduling, usage metering and control-electronics interfaces.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Standardizing the operations stack lowers integration cost for new hardware vendors.
insights.locator: qBraid OS Platform Infrastructure and GPU Simulation Benchmarks

insights.claim: Early-access hardware vendors for qBraid OS listed in the article are Diraq, Quobly, IBM, MemQ, Quantum Machines, Equal1 and IonQ.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Broad vendor roster suggests qBraid is aiming for a neutral control-plane position.

insights.claim: By integrating NVIDIA CUDA-Q and NVQLink, qBraid OS lets classical GPU nodes perform real-time quantum error-correction decoding and classical co-processing during active QPU execution, with sub-millisecond QEC decoding.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: NVIDIA is entrenching GPUs in the QEC loop, expanding its addressable market in quantum.
insights.locator: By integrating NVIDIA CUDA-Q and NVQLink

insights.claim: Operational workflows and system setup in qBraid OS can be automated by AI coding agents within operator-defined permission boundaries.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Agentic automation of quantum facility operations is an emerging angle.
insights.locator: By integrating NVIDIA CUDA-Q and NVQLink

insights.claim: qBraid launched two hosted simulators on NVIDIA GH200 Grace Hopper Superchips in its Leo cluster: gpu-sv, an exact state-vector simulator up to 35 qubits, and gpu-tn, a tensor-network simulator for weakly entangled circuits up to 500 qubits.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: GPU-hosted simulation is a cheap on-ramp that keeps developers inside the NVIDIA stack.
insights.locator: In tandem, qBraid launched two hosted

insights.claim: On a 32-qubit random circuit 20 layers deep, gpu-sv ran in 2.7 seconds on a GH200 node versus 2 minutes 43 seconds across 32 CPU server cores.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Roughly 60x speedup quantifies the GPU advantage for circuit validation before QPU submission.

insights.claim: gpu-sv reaches 35 qubits by storing amplitudes beyond the GPU's 96 GB HBM3 limit (33 qubits single precision) in the 72-core Grace CPU's RAM over the coherent CPU-to-GPU interconnect, without manual configuration.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Memory architecture, not just compute, sets practical simulation limits.

insights.claim: gpu-tn uses matrix product state representations with default bond dimension 64 and drops low-weight entanglement contributions above configurable maxBondDim thresholds to reach 500 qubits on wide, low-entanglement circuits.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Tensor-network simulation is only valid for weakly entangled circuits, limiting its use for benchmarking hard problems.
